answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to verifiable inertial telemetry recorded during a physical voyage. Each participant binds an execution thread to an onboard security kernel that continuously signs timestamped movement vectors. An attacker incurs the verifiable physical cost of fabricating and propelling real navigation hardware per identity. However, cumulative sensor drift can distort genuine motion paths, leading to false-positive rejections of honest nodes.
